subject: Auron Labs urgent batch: temporary dedicated GPU tranche request
messages:
From: Sylvia Ho <sylvia.ho@auron.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@auron.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Urgent: batch spike next week — temporary dedicated tranche request

Hi Priya,

Quick context — we just signed a strategic retail partner and their onboarding workload will start a controlled production batch on Feb 23. Forecasted token use for the 72-hour onboarding window is ~3x our normal peak. Our existing reserved commit covers only 8 A100-equivalent GPUs and will not cover the spike.

Can Redwood provide a temporary dedicated tranche (40 GPUs) for Feb 23 00:00 UTC through Feb 26 00:00 UTC? We understand this is outside our committed sku; Auron is happy to discuss credits or a short-term add-on fee. This is time-sensitive because our partner onboarding is a hard milestone.

Attachments: batch_forecast_q1.pdf (pdf) — short forecast and partner SLA.

Please let me know next steps or if you need a call.

Thanks,
Sylvia Ho
Head of Platform Ops
Auron Labs
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Sylvia Ho <sylvia.ho@auron.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Feb 2028 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: batch spike next week — temporary dedicated tranche request

Hi Sylvia — thanks for the heads-up and the forecast.

Short answer: we can help, but we need to balance existing reserved commitments and SLAs for other customers. Options I can mobilize quickly: 

- Option A — Temporary tranche: carve 40 GPUs from our burst pool and place behind a hard cap for the 72h window. This will incur a short-term add-on fee; I can share pricing immediately. Attach: proposed_tranche_plan.xlsx (xlsx).
- Option B — Partial tranche + prioritized scheduling: provide 24 GPUs dedicated, plus guaranteed burst queues for an additional 16 GPUs with best-effort latency guarantees. Lower cost but higher variability.
- Option C — Deferral + expedited migration support: keep your 8 reserved GPUs and accelerate quantization/parallelization work (we can assign an infra team member) to reduce peak needs. No tranche, less disruptive.

What I need from you by EOD today: confirmation of estimated absolute GPU-hours (not just multiple), whether Auron can accept a credit or commit to an upsell after the window, and who will be on the call if we need to escalate.

I’ve looped in Karthik and Ben so they can weigh in on trade-offs (pricing vs risk). If you prefer, we can do a 20-min call at 2pm PT.

— Priya
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Feb 2028 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: batch spike next week — temporary dedicated tranche request

On Tue, Feb 20, 2028 at 10:05 AM Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Short answer: we can help, but we need to balance existing reserved commitments and SLAs for other customers.

Quick internal note: we are ~75% committed in the burst pool for Feb 23–26 already (see CAP-478). Carving 40 GPUs will materially increase reprovision risk for other high-priority customers (Lucent and Nimbus have canary runs that week).

Proposed internal approach:
- Run a prioritization matrix (impact x contractual commitment). Auron = strategic, but committed $/gpu-month is low relative to some enterprise contracts.
- If we do a full tranche, require a balancing concession: either (a) a one-time credit (to offset our opportunity cost) or (b) move Auron to a higher reserved tier post-window (30–60 day notice) with minimum term.
- If only partial tranche (Option B), plan to shift scheduled non-critical batch windows for lower-tier customers to reclaim burst headroom. That requires ops coordination — Markus to confirm feasibility.

Ben — thoughts on commercial terms? Markus — can ops deliver 24 dedicated GPUs reliably with current scheduling?

— Karthik
Director, Capacity Planning
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Feb 2028 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: batch spike next week — temporary dedicated tranche request

Agree with Karthik. Commercially we should push for an uplift — short-term add-on fee + commitment to a follow-on reserved tranche (minimum 3 months) if Auron wants guaranteed scale going forward. Given the strategic nature of the partner, offering a discounted uplift in exchange for the long-term commitment feels fair.

Markus — can you confirm ops lead time to provision 24 GPUs and what the expected risk is to other scheduled runs? If provisioning is sub-24h then we can do Option B immediately; full 40 GPUs will require several schedule shifts and approval from the capacity council.

— Ben
VP, Sales Operations
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Feb 2028 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: batch spike next week — temporary dedicated tranche request

Update from ops: we can reliably carve out 24 GPUs from our burst pool and enforce a hard cap on them for Feb 23–25 without impacting enterprise canaries if we also shift two lower-priority nightly runs (we already have a likely swap candidate). Full 40 GPUs would require preempting one enterprise run and escalating to the capacity council — lead time ~6–8 hours to coordinate and run safety checks.

I recommend we offer Option B (24 dedicated + 16 best-effort burst) as the default immediate response and request the commercial uplift/commitment Karthik/Ben suggested. If Auron insists on 40 we escalate.

-Markus
Head of Infrastructure Operations
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Sylvia Ho <sylvia.ho@auron.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, procurement@auron.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Feb 2028 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: batch spike next week — temporary dedicated tranche request

Hi Sylvia — thanks for the rapid reply. Hands-on summary and decision: 

- Immediate allocation: we will provision 24 dedicated GPUs for Auron from Feb 23 00:00 UTC through Feb 25 23:59 UTC. Those GPUs will be behind a hard cap and isolated from best-effort preemption.
- Burst support: we will also enable best-effort access to an additional 16 GPUs from the burst pool; these are not guaranteed and subject to higher latency.
- Commercials: one-time add-on fee (we’ll send a quote) plus a conditional commitment: if Auron executes a 3-month reserved upgrade within 30 days after the window, we will credit 50% of the one-time fee back. Draft terms attached: capacity_trade_terms-draft.docx (docx).
- Ops notes: Markus confirmed the carve-out will not impact enterprise canaries provided we shift two lower-priority nightly runs.

Next steps: please confirm by EOD if this arrangement works; if so we will: (1) send a formal quote and DocuSign addendum, (2) provision 24 GPUs, and (3) schedule a 30-min runbook call with your ops lead to finalize handoffs.

If you need the full 40 GPUs we can escalate immediately to the capacity council but will need a written sign-off from your procurement accepting premium surge pricing and a waiver for potential scheduled run adjustments.

Thanks — Priya
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
